text: σπουδαῖος, eager, zealous; earnest.
σπουδαίως, eagerly, zealously; earnestly.
σπυρίς, see σφυρίς.
στάδιος, στάδιον, a stade, a measurement of distance about twelve yards short of a furlong, or about 180–200 metres.
στάμνος, an earthenware pot (jar).
στασιαστής, a revolutionary.
στατήρ, a stater, that is four drachmae (which see), temple-tax for two persons.
σταφυλή, a grape.
στάχυς, an ear (spike) of corn.
Στάχυς, a Christian man at Rome.
στέγη (originally poetical), a roof; in Mk. ii 4 perhaps of thatch.
στέγω, (a) I roof over, cover: hence, I conceal, hide, but not in N.T.; (b) I keep out (weather): hence, I keep close, put up with, endure patiently, bear up under.
στεῖρα, a barren (childless) woman.
στέλλω (originally, I set, place: hence, I bring together, make compact; then, I restrain, check), mid. I draw (shrink) back from anything.
στέμμα (from στέφω, I wreathe), a garland.
στεναγμός, a groan.
στενάζω, I groan.
στενός, narrow.
στενοχωρέω (στενός and χῶρος, cf. English colloquial, I keep some one in a tight place), I press upon, cramp, restrain.
στενοχωρία (lit. confinement in a narrow space), restriction, restraint; anguish, great trouble.
στερεός, solid; firm, lit. or met.
στερεόω, I make firm, or solid: met., Ac. xvi 5.
στερέωμα (probably a military metaphor), firm foundation, bulwark.
Στεφανᾶς (a pet form of Στεφανηφόρος), Stephanas, a Corinthian Christian.
Στέφανος, Stephen, one of the seven original ‘deacons’ at Jerusalem, and the first martyr.
gloss: Stephen, one of the seven original ‘deacons’ at Jerusalem

text: στεφανόω, I wreathe, crown as victor, 2 Tim. ii 5, hence met.
στῆθος, the breast.
στηριγμός, support.
στιβάς, a wisp (bundle) of brushwood, twigs or other light growth.
gloss: a wisp (bundle) of brushwood, twigs or other light growth

text: στίγμα, properly, a brand burned into, or the mark of a cut made in, the skin of a slave; in Gal. vi 17 τὰ στίγματα are the marks or scars, due to the lictor’s rods at Pisidian Antioch and the stones at Lystra, marking Paul as the slave of Jesus.
gloss: a brand burned into, or the mark of a cut made in, the skin of a slave

text: στιγμή (lit. a pricking), an instant, a moment.
στίλβω, I gleam, flash.
στοά, a portico, colonnade, porch: that ‘of Solomon’ was on the East side of the Temple.

στοιχεῖον (elementum), (a) plur. the heavenly bodies, 2 Pet. iii 10, 12; (b) a rudiment, an element, a rudimentary principle, an elementary rule; but in Gal. iv 3 there is much to be said for taking the word in the sense of spirit, demon (possibly also in (a)).
στοιχέω, I walk (properly, in a straight line, in rank).
στόμαχος, the stomach.
στρατεία, military service, used met.
στράτευμα, an army, a body of soldiers.
gloss: an army, a body of soldiers

text: στρατεύομαι, I serve in the army, I am in the army, I am a soldier (whether on active service or not): hence met. I make war, I take up war, e.g. 1 Pet. ii 11.
gloss: I serve in the army, I am in the army, I am a soldier

text: στρατιά, an army.
στρατολογέω, tr., I enrol in the army.
στρατόπεδον, a camp.
στρεβλόω, (lit. I twist, warp, stretch on the rack, hence met.) I twist, strain.
στρηνιάω, I am wanton, I wanton.
στρῆνος, wantonness, luxury.
στρουθίον, a sparrow, the cheapest of all birds for food.
στρώννυμι, στρωννύω (sterno), I spread out, strew; in Mk. xiv 15, Lk. xxii 12 of the dining couches with the cushions ready for diners, cf. Ac. ix 34 of making one’s bed.
στυγητός, hated, hateful.
στυγνάζω, (a) I am sad, Mk. x 22; (b) I am dull (overcast), Mt. xvi 3.
στύλος, a pillar for supporting an entablature or other structure; hence metaph.
gloss: a pillar for supporting an entablature or other structure

text: συγγένεια, collective, all the συγγενεῖς, kindred, kin, relations.
συγγενίς, a kinswoman.
συγγνώμη, see συνγνώμη.
συγκυρία, coincidence, chance.
σύγχυσις, confusion, disturbance.
συκάμινος (a Semitic word), the black mulberry tree.
συκομορέα, a sycamore tree.
σῦκον, a fig.
συκοφαντέω (calumnior), I accuse falsely.
συλαγωγέω, I take away from as booty (plunder), I rob.
gloss: I take away from as booty (plunder), I rob

text: συλάω, I rob.
συλλέγω, I collect, gather together.
συλλογίζομαι, I reason together with others.
συμβουλεύω, act. I advise: mid. συμβουλευόμεθα, we counsel one another.
συμβούλιον (consilium), (a) a body of advisers (assessors) in a court, a council, Ac. xxv 12; (b) abstr., consultation, counsel, advice; resolution, decree: διδόναι (Aramaism) Mk. iii 6.
gloss: a body of advisers (assessors) in a court, a council

text: σύμβουλος, an adviser.

Συμεών, Symeon, (a) the patriarch, son of Jacob and founder of a tribe, Rev. vii 7; (b) an ancestor of Jesus, Lk. iii 30; (c) an inhabitant of Jerusalem, who blessed the babe Jesus, Lk. ii 25, 34; (d) an Antiochian Christian, also called Niger, Ac. xiii 1; (e) a form of the Hebrew name of Peter the Apostle, Ac. xv 14, 2 Pet. i 1 (v.l.).
συμμορφίζω (συνμ.), lit. I cause to share the form (see μορφή) of another, hence in Phil. iii 10 συνμορφιζόμενος = being made to share the experience of.
gloss: I cause to share the form (see μορφή) of another

text: σύμμορφος, sharing the form of another.
συμπαθής, sharing the experiences of others.
συμπόσιον, properly a drinking bout, following dinner: συμπόσια συμπόσια (colloquial), in companies of diners.
σύμφορος, advantageous: τὸ σύμφορον, as substantive.
συμφυλέτης, a fellow tribesman, one of the same tribe, doubtless with reference to Jews in Thessalonica, all enrolled in one city-tribe.
gloss: a fellow tribesman, one of the same tribe

text: σύμφυτος, grown along with, vitally one with, united with.
gloss: grown along with, vitally one with, united with

text: συμφώνησις, harmony, agreement.
συμφωνία, bagpipes (cf. Dan. iii 5), but perhaps music, symphony.
σύμφωνος, agreeing: ἐκ συμφώνου, by agreement.
συμψηφίζω, I calculate together, I reckon up.
gloss: I calculate together, I reckon up

text: συναγωνίζομαι, I struggle (contend) in company with.
συναθλέω, I compete together with others, originally of athletic contests, and then met.
συναθροίζω, tr. I gather together, assemble.
συναίρω; with λόγον, I compare (settle) accounts, make a reckoning.
gloss: I compare (settle) accounts, make a reckoning

text: συναιχμάλωτος, a fellow-captive, a fellow-prisoner, a companion in chains.
gloss: a fellow-captive, a fellow-prisoner, a companion in chains

text: συνακολουθέω, I accompany.
συνᾰλίζομαι (from σύν and ἅλς, ‘salt’), I have table fellowship with, I share a common meal with. (Others take as συνᾱλίζομαι (from σύν and ἁλής, ‘crowded’), I meet with, from time to time.)
gloss: I have table fellowship with, I share a common meal with
note: breathing/accent marks on ἅλς and ἁλής are blurred on the image (read as rough breathing); quantity marks ᾰ and ᾱ on the two forms of the headword as printed | approved by David, 2026-11-09

text: συναλλάσσω, I attempt (seek) to reconcile.
συναναβαίνω, I go up with.
συναναμίγνυμι, mid. I associate intimately with.
συναναπαύομαι, I rest along with.
συναντάω, I meet, encounter: in Ac. xx 22, with inanimate subject.
συναντιλαμβάνομαι, I lend a hand along with, I take interest in (a thing) along with (others), I assist jointly to perform some task, I co-operate with, I take my share in.
gloss: I lend a hand along with

text: συναπάγω, I lead away with, I carry along with (in good or bad sense according to context): mid. c. dat., I condescend to, Rom. xii 16.
gloss: I lead away with, I carry along with

text: συναποθνήσκω, I die along with, I die together (with others).
gloss: I die along with, I die together (with others)

text: συναπόλλυμαι, I perish along with.
συναποστέλλω, I send away in some one’s company.
gloss: I send away in some one’s company

text: συναρμολογέω (an architectural term, ἁρμός meaning ‘the side of a stone’, and -λογεῖν added by analogy with λιθολόγος without its proper force), I fit together (by means of all the elaborate preparatory processes necessary).
συναρπάζω, I keep a firm grip of.
gloss: I keep a firm grip of

text: συνβασιλεύω, I reign along with (together with) another, I am a king with, in met. sense.
gloss: I reign along with (together with) another

text: συνβιβάζω, (a) I bring together, join, unite, Eph. iv 16, Col. ii 19; (b) I put together, compare, examine closely, hence I consider, conclude, Ac. xvi 10; I deduce, prove, Ac. ix 22; (c) (a Biblical sense, translation Greek) I teach, instruct, Ac. xix 33 (v.l.), 1 Cor. ii 16, Col. ii 2.
σύνδεσμος, a binding together, a means of holding together, a bond, lit. and met.: in Ac. viii 23 the man is in (εἰς = ἐν) the grip of ἀδικία.
gloss: a binding together, a means of holding together, a bond

text: συνδοξάζω, I glorify along with.
συνδρομή, a running together, a tumultuous concourse.
gloss: a running together, a tumultuous concourse

text: συνεγείρω, I raise along with the Messiah (from the dead, or from a dead spiritual state).
gloss: I raise along with the Messiah

text: σύνειμι, I go with, I accompany, Lk. viii 4.
note: first of two σύνειμι entries (from εἶμι)

text: σύνειμι, I am with, I am in company with, I company with.
gloss: I am with, I am in company with, I company with
note: second of two σύνειμι entries (from εἰμί)

text: συνεισέρχομαι, I go in with, I enter with.
gloss: I go in with, I enter with

text: συνέκδημος, a travelling-companion.
συνεκλεκτός, fellow-chosen, fellow-elect, understand ἐκκλησία.
συνεπιμαρτυρέω, I add my testimony to that already given.
gloss: I add my testimony to that already given

text: συνεπιτίθεμαι (lit. I join in attacking), I join in the charge.
συνέπομαι, I accompany.
συνεσθίω, I eat in company with.
συνετός (lit. one who can put things together, from συνίημι), intelligent; in Mt. xi 25, Lk. x. 21 it doubtless refers to Pharisees learned in the law.
συνευωχέομαι, I feast along with.
συνεφίστημι: 2 aor. intr. (the multitude) rose up together, set upon together.
gloss: rose up together, set upon together

text: συνζητητής, a discusser, debater.
σύνζυγος, yoke-fellow, companion, colleague (perhaps a proper name).
συνζωοποιέω, I make living along with.
συνήδομαι, I delight in.
συνήθεια, custom, habit: c. gen. habituation to, intercourse with, familiarity with, 1 Cor. viii 7.
συνηλικιώτης, a contemporary.
συνθάπτω, I bury along with.
συνθλάω, I break in pieces, break completely.
gloss: I break in pieces, break completely

text: συνθλίβω, I press closely upon, hustle.
συνθρύπτω (lit. I crush to pieces), I weaken thoroughly, unman.
συνκάθημαι, I am sitting (seated) with: in Ac. xxvi 30, perhaps to be compared with English assessor.
συνκαθίζω, (a) tr. I cause to sit along with; (b) intr. I sit in company (together).
gloss: I cause to sit along with

text: συνκακοπαθέω, I am ill treated along with, I take my share of suffering (in 2 Tim. i 8 the dat. is not governed by συν, but = for the benefit of).
gloss: I am ill treated along with, I take my share of suffering

text: συνκακουχέω, I treat evilly (with hardship) along with.
gloss: I treat evilly (with hardship) along with

text: συνκαλύπτω, I veil (cover) completely.
συνκάμπτω, I bend low, I cause to stoop low.
gloss: I bend low, I cause to stoop low

text: συνκαταβαίνω, I come down along with (together).
συνκατάθεσις, agreement, union.
συνκατατίθεμαι, I agree with.
συνκαταψηφίζω, I number (reckon) along with.
συνκεράννυμι, (a) I mix together, compound, 1 Cor. xii 24; (b) pass. with dat. of instrument (πίστει), I agree with, Heb. iv 2 (reading acc. plur.).
συνκινέω, I stir violently.
συνκλείω, I shut together; I enclose, I shut in on all sides, e.g. Rom. xi 32.
συνκληρονόμος, a joint heir, a fellow heir.
gloss: a joint heir, a fellow heir

text: συνκοινωνέω, I have partnership in, I share in (with others).
gloss: I have partnership in, I share in

text: συνκοινωνός, a fellow sharer (in), a joint partaker (of).
gloss: a fellow sharer (in), a joint partaker (of)

text: συνκομίζω, I carry (convey) together, i.e. to burial; or I take up for burial; hence I bury (cf. effero): perhaps, however, I get back, recover (the συν- expressing the collecting of the mangled remains).
συνκρίνω, I compare.
συνκύπτω, I am bent double, bent in two, bowed down.
gloss: I am bent double, bent in two, bowed down

text: συνλαλέω, I speak together (with).
συνλυπέομαι, I am greatly pained (grieved).
συνμαθητής, a fellow disciple, a fellow scholar.
gloss: a fellow disciple, a fellow scholar

text: συνμαρτυρέω, I join in giving evidence (bearing witness) with.
gloss: I join in giving evidence (bearing witness) with

text: συνμερίζω, I cause to share with (in the sacrifices).
συνμέτοχος, a fellow sharer, a partner.
συνμιμητής, a joint imitator, an imitator along (together) with others.
gloss: a joint imitator, an imitator along (together) with others

text: συνοδεύω, I journey (travel) along with.
συνοδία, a travelling company, caravan.
σύνοιδα (conscius sum), I share knowledge with another, I am privy to anything. In fact the word especially implies consciousness of guilt, e.g. 1 Cor. iv 4.
gloss: I share knowledge with another, I am privy to anything

text: συνοικέω, I cohabit with, live in wedlock with.
gloss: I cohabit with, live in wedlock with

text: συνοικοδομέω, met. I build together.
συνομιλέω, I talk with.
συνομορέω, I am contiguous with, I am next door to.
gloss: I am contiguous with, I am next door to

text: συνοχή (lit. compression; then narrowness), met. anxiety.
συνπαθέω, I suffer along with.
συνπαραγίνομαι, I arrive along with.
συνπαρακαλέω, I cheer (encourage) along with.
συνπαραλαμβάνω, I take along with me (as helper).
gloss: I take along with me (as helper)

text: συνπάρειμι, I am present (here) along with.
συνπάσχω, I suffer together.
συνπέμπω, I send along with.
συνπεριλαμβάνω, I embrace closely.
συνπίνω, I drink (wine) along with.
συνπίπτω, I fall together, I fall in, I collapse.
gloss: I fall together, I fall in, I collapse

text: συνπληρόω, (a) I fill up, hence pass., by an idiom analogous to English, συνεπληροῦντο, Lk. viii 23, they were filling up (where it was really the ship that was filling up); (b) (Hebraistic) I complete, of the coming to an end of an interval of days before some event (in Ac. ii 1 the day of the event may be partly included).
συνπνίγω, met. I choke utterly: in Lk. viii 42 by exaggeration (possibly slang), of pressing very hard upon, hustling, in a crowd (cf. the more correct συνθλίβω).
συνπολίτης, a fellow-citizen.
συνπορεύομαι, I journey with, I go with; I go together.
gloss: I journey with, I go with

text: συνπρεσβύτερος, a fellow-elder.
συνσ., see συσσ.
note: the entry on p. 258 (printed 251) is the cross-reference 'συνσ., see συσσ.', not συνιστάνω; συνιστάνω appears only as a variant headword of συνίστημι on p. 256 (printed 249)

text: συνστέλλω, (a) I wrap round, swathe in a sort of winding-sheet, or possibly, I lay out, Ac. v 6; (b) I contract, compress; hence I shorten, 1 Cor. vii 29.
gloss: I wrap round, swathe in a sort of winding-sheet
